name: Do You Need an Electrical Panel Upgrade for a Kitchen Remodel or ADU?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to upgrade my electrical panel for a kitchen remodel or ADU?
mainEntity.text: Do I need to upgrade my electrical panel for a kitchen remodel or ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: An electrical panel upgrade is common in kitchen remodels and ADU projects, but it is not automatic. The need depends on the existing service size, the appliance load, whether gas equipment is being replaced with electric equipment, and whether the project adds significant new circuits or a separate dwelling unit. Older homes often have panels that are already near capacity, so a new kitchen layout, induction range, electric water heating, or ADU mechanical equipment can push the system beyond what it can safely support. A licensed electrician or contractor should evaluate the existing panel early and determine whether a subpanel, service upgrade, or full replacement is needed. This step matters because panel work can affect the schedule, permit scope, and utility coordination. If you are planning a remodel or ADU, ask for an electrical assessment before finalizing the design so you do not discover a major power limitation after demolition has started.
acceptedAnswer.description: You may need a panel upgrade if the existing panel does not have enough capacity for new appliances, HVAC, lighting, or added dwelling space. Older panels often become a bottleneck during kitchen remodels and ADU projects. A load calculation and inspection of the existing service should be done early.
